executive_summary: Apollo Micro Systems is scaling defence electronics and expanding toward complete systems and explosives. September earnings growth is strong, but the very long working-capital cycle and acquisition/capex commitments mean reported order visibility is not yet equivalent to cash-generating visibility.
research_stance: Rapid defence scale-up, with cash conversion and acquisition integration still the decisive risks.
results_analysis: The local consolidated September 2026 quarter records revenue ₹388.00 crore, operating profit ₹111.00 crore and PAT ₹46.00 crore. Revenue changed +72.4% YoY and +54.6% QoQ; PAT changed +53.3% YoY and +84.0% QoQ.

Operating profit changed +88.1% YoY and +105.6% QoQ. The calculated operating-profit/sales margin is 28.61%, versus 26.22% a year earlier and 21.51% in June. These calculations use a consistently rounded local series; management EBITDA may use a different scope or definition.

FY26 CFO was minus ₹130 crore and free cash flow minus ₹357 crore. The current call reports H1 CFO positive ₹22 crore, but working capital remained 353 days, only modestly better than 359 in FY26. Management described FY29 as the point for sustained positive quarterly operating cash flow as production orders rise.

Price and financial dates differ: the cleaned close used here is ₹440.10 on 2026-11-12; the public-financial snapshot is dated 2026-11-13. The screenshot price is not treated as a live or verified valuation input. Local public-financial-data parquets, September 2026 quarter; amounts rounded to ₹ crore.

Audit finding: management describes 40% year-on-year group PAT growth, while the local ₹46 crore versus ₹30 crore comparison gives 53.3%. The current rupee amount agrees but the comparative base remains unresolved. Standalone PAT ₹48 crore exceeds consolidated PAT ₹46 crore, so integration is not yet clearly profit-accretive.

valuation.method: Reverse valuation and cash-earnings constraints; no unsupported point target
valuation.assessment: At about 116× available trailing EPS, valuation requires a major earnings and cash scale-up. Long working capital, integration losses, expansion commitments and uncertain normal taxation make a simple P/E target weak. Order expectations need scope, timing, funding and execution analysis.
assumptions: At the 12 November adjusted close of ₹440.10, the available four-quarter EPS sum is ₹3.79, implying approximately 116.1× earnings and a 0.86% earnings yield. This is a price/available-EPS calculation, not a forecast or a fully normalized multiple.

A 20% contraction in the earnings multiple would require 25% cumulative EPS growth merely to keep the share price unchanged; dividends are excluded. This is algebraic sensitivity, not a prediction of the exit multiple.
A point value needs electronics versus explosives cash economics, diluted capital, acquisition funding and normal taxation; those bridges remain incomplete.

business_economics: Electronics, explosives and complete systems have different customers, capital requirements and cash cycles. Standalone Q2 PAT of ₹48 crore exceeds group PAT of ₹46 crore despite lower revenue, showing that subsidiary scale currently creates a profit drag.

The ₹1,765 crore group order book differs from standalone visibility of a little below ₹1,300 crore. Development programmes, limited-series work and production awards require different forecasts. Trials and management confidence are not executed orders.
earnings_quality: Current revenue ₹388 crore, EBITDA ₹111 crore and PAT ₹46 crore agree with local rounded rows. The call’s 40% PAT-growth description does not match 53.3% on the local comparative base. Matching the current amount does not verify the growth percentage.

Positive H1 CFO of ₹22 crore improves on FY26’s negative ₹130 crore, but 353 working-capital days remains very long. Management points to FY29 for consistently positive quarterly cash conversion as production orders expand; the current half-year is not a completed turnaround.
capital_allocation: Premier funding and completion, Ideal/IDL improvement and new systems capacity require cash before the expanded opportunity becomes recurring shareholder income. Acquired scale should be tested through subsidiary profit, cash and capital deployed.

A question about an effective tax rate near 51% receives a discussion of a 25% to 30% statutory change but no complete bridge. Neither a low normal tax assumption nor a permanent 50% rate should be inserted without reconciliation.
valuation_logic: An approximately 116× price/available-EPS ratio leaves a high burden of proof. Strong revenue growth alone is insufficient if collections, subsidiary returns, dilution and tax do not improve together.

A valuation should separate existing electronics cash earnings, explosives turnaround and prospective systems programmes, then account for incremental funding. Conditional ₹4,500–5,000 crore order-book language is not cash or guaranteed annual sales.
peer_positioning: Electronics peers help assess qualification, production conversion and receivables. Explosives peers suit Ideal/IDL, while complete-system vendors operate at another scope. One defence-sector multiple conceals these distinctions.
Government programme exposure can support demand visibility while leaving award, acceptance and collection risk. Compare order-to-cash and incremental returns rather than only order-book growth.
